topic: Rent vs buy and the 5% rule
hook: Renting is throwing money away, right?

blocks.narration: Renting is throwing money away, right? Not so fast. Owning a home has money you never get back too.
blocks.visual: Tilt-shift miniature street with a renter's apartment and a house side by side

blocks.narration: Renters lose their rent each month. Owners lose costs too, and a simple rule of thumb estimates them at about five percent a year.
blocks.visual: Coins drift away from both buildings into the sky at a similar pace

blocks.narration: Roughly one percent for property taxes, one percent for maintenance and repairs, and about three percent for the cost of capital.
blocks.visual: Three small coin streams labeled with tiny icons: a tax building, a wrench, and a growing plant

blocks.narration: Cost of capital means the return your down payment and equity could have earned if invested instead, plus mortgage interest.
blocks.visual: A down payment bag sits beside a ghostly investment jar that could have been growing

blocks.narration: On a five hundred thousand dollar home, five percent is about twenty-five thousand dollars a year, or roughly two thousand eighty-three a month.
blocks.visual: A tiny calendar flips twelve pages while a coin pile forms beside the house

blocks.narration: If you can rent a similar home for less than that, renting and investing the difference may come out ahead financially.
blocks.visual: The renter drops spare coins into a growing investment jar each month

blocks.narration: If rent costs more, buying may win. Local prices, how long you will stay, and interest rates change the answer a lot.
blocks.visual: A balance scale on a rooftop tilts one way, then the other, as small clouds pass

blocks.narration: It is a starting point, not a final verdict. Comment your city and whether renting or buying wins there right now.
blocks.visual: Camera rises above the miniature town, lights flickering on in both homes

cta: Comment your city and whether renting or buying wins there.

captions.hook_line: Is renting really throwing money away? Try the 5% rule 🔑
captions.body: A popular rule of thumb estimates the yearly unrecoverable costs of owning at about 5% of the home's value: property tax, maintenance and the cost of capital. On a $500,000 home that is about $25,000 a year, or roughly $2,083 a month. It is a rough guide, not a verdict.
